What listing costs you

Nothing. The rancher pays no listing fee, no subscription and no placement charge — the tag sells on its own page, to someone who arrived looking for that unit.

Funds are held until the tag is verified. The verification is named on the listing, so the buyer is looking at a check, not at an adjective, and you are not answering the same question six times.

Call 936-287-3304 See what buyers see →
  1. Tell us the unit, the species and the number of tags. One call is enough.
  2. The tag gets a page, a price and a verification state — and the unit guide starts showing it.
  3. Buyers reserve through LandownerTags; funds sit in escrow until the tag clears.
  4. You are paid on release, and the listing comes down the same day it sells.

Questions ranchers ask first

The four that decide whether a first listing happens.

Do I have to know what it is worth?
No. You name a price or ask for one; either way it is your number that goes on the page, and the ledger shows you what comparable units are listing at this week.
What happens if it does not sell?
The listing comes down and the unit page keeps counting demand, so next season you are deciding with a number instead of a hunch. There is no cost to having listed.
Who sees my name and my ranch?
The unit, species and price are public because that is what a buyer searches. Your contact details are not — buyers call one number, and that number is answered.
How fast does the money move?
Funds are held in escrow at reservation and released when the tag is verified. Nothing on the Hunters Domain side takes a payment, so there is one place the money sits and one rule for releasing it.

A person answers, in season and out.

The tag desk is run by Jimmy Horton and it is staffed fourteen hours a day. A rancher who calls gets a decision, not a ticket — and a buyer who calls gets the listing record opened on the call.
